name: Lupinus

project_scope.note: Genus lesson structurally live; species installation remains species-lane work.

recognition.where_to_look_first: Start with the palmately compound leaf: several narrow leaflets radiate from one point. Then confirm a dense raceme of papilionoid flowers and a legume pod.
vegetative: leaflets radiating from one petiole tip
recognition.local_anchor: Lupinus texensis — Texas bluebonnet source concept; prior project text/diagnostics exist but canonical installation is independent.

comparisons.rule: Lupinus commonly shows palmately compound leaves; Baptisia commonly has trifoliolate leaves and inflated/ovoid pods.
Dermatophyllum secundiflorum is woody and evergreen with pinnate glossy leaves; local Lupinus is herbaceous with palmate leaves.

visual_needs: whole plant and palmate leaf architecture
